decisions.reason: By 2022 much uncertainty has resolved, but this drain housing line remains close to the firm's core drainage technology and compatible product-family logic, so keeping it is still the better option.
As a flagship designer shower drainage line that fits the firm's strategic direction toward integrated, design-conscious bathroom solutions, it would be very unlikely to be withdrawn now.

This integrated shower element still supports the firm's push into low-profile and accessible shower installations, so management would likely retain it even though its market potential should now be clearer.
The backflow-protected basement drain serves a clear technical problem in a related niche, and for a German specialist drainage firm that makes it worth continuing unless performance is clearly poor.

After several years the option value of this more peripheral valve line is likely largely exhausted, and resources are better redeployed to the firm's stronger core drainage systems and new development.
